title: Headache
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with severe headache, fever, photophobia, nuchal rigidity, and altered mental status. Exam reveals positive Kernig's sign (pain with knee extension when hip flexed 90°) and Brudzinski's sign (involuntary hip/knee flexion with passive neck flexion). Petechial/purpuric rash is present — meningococcemia causes DIC and purpura fulminans. This is a medical emergency. Do NOT delay antibiotics for CT or LP. Blood cultures + LP with CSF analysis (opening pressure, cell count with differential, glucose, protein, Gram stain, culture). CSF: neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose (<40 or <2/3 serum), elevated protein, Gram-negative diplococci. Empiric antibiotics: ceftriaxone 2g IV + vancomycin + dexamethasone (before or with first dose). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk (age >50, immunocompromised). Droplet precautions for meningococcal. Chemoprophylaxis for close contacts (rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone).
chief_complaint: Severe headache, fever, stiff neck, photophobia, rash

stacks.finding: Petechiae in >50% of meningococcemia — non-blanching purple spots. Purpura fulminans.

stacks.label: CT head (if indicated before LP)
stacks.finding: If papilledema, focal neuro deficit, AMS, seizure, immunocompromised — CT before LP to rule out mass effect.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP
stacks.finding: Screening. Hyponatremia in SIADH from meningitis.

stacks.label: PT/PTT / INR
stacks.finding: Assess for DIC — meningococcemia can trigger DIC.

stacks.label: Ceftriaxone IV
stacks.finding: [Auto-split from bundled label "Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Vancomycin IV"] Empiric: ceftriaxone (covers N. meningitidis) + vancomycin (covers resistant S. pneumoniae). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk.

stacks.label: Vancomycin IV
stacks.finding: [Auto-split from bundled label "Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Vancomycin IV"] Empiric: ceftriaxone (covers N. meningitidis) + vancomycin (covers resistant S. pneumoniae). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk.

stacks.label: Dexamethasone IV
stacks.finding: Before or with first antibiotics. Reduces hearing loss and neurologic sequelae in S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae meningitis.

stacks.label: Droplet precautions
stacks.finding: Meningococcal meningitis requires droplet isolation until 24h of effective antibiotics.

stacks.label: Admit to ICU
stacks.finding: Bacterial meningitis requires ICU for close monitoring and IV antibiotics.

physical_exam.neurological: Nuchal rigidity. Kernig's sign positive. Brudzinski's sign positive. Altered mental status. No focal deficits.
physical_exam.skin: Petechial rash — non-blanching purple spots suggesting meningococcemia.

decoys.label: Delay antibiotics for CT/LP results
decoys.reason_wrong: NEVER delay antibiotics in suspected bacterial meningitis. Blood cultures first, then immediate empiric antibiotics. LP after stabilization. Mortality increases with each hour of delay.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Bacterial = low glucose (CSF:serum <0.4) + high protein + neutrophils >1000. Viral = normal glucose + lymphocytes. Fungal/TB = low glucose + lymphocytes.
Do NOT delay. Dexamethasone before/with first dose reduces neurologic sequelae. Droplet precautions. Chemoprophylaxis for contacts.

case_summary: Bacterial meningitis (meningococcal). Triad: headache + fever + nuchal rigidity + petechiae. CSF: neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose. Ceftriaxone + vanc + dexamethasone immediately. Droplet precautions. ICU.
